each dredging region, and gross yardage per each disposal location.

separately for each dredge;
c. A utility summary sheet that lists every utility (for both the
dredging channel and disposal areas). For every utility, the
following verified information shall be provided: C/L station (for New
Orleans Harbor, the 100' or 160' offset B/L station, whichever is
applicable), C/L XY-coordinate (for New Orleans Harbor, the 100' or
160' offset B/L XY-coordinate, whichever is applicable), right
descending bank toe XY-coordinate, left descending bank toe
XY-coordinate, minimum elevation, all horizontal information required
to determine actual alignments of all utilities, utility size, utility
type, and POC information. In the notes column, state whether the
utilities were dredged over, disposed on, skipped (state reason why),
and any issues with the utility owner. A sample utility summary sheet
is included at the end of this section. If the Contractor worked in
multiple dredging regions, the Contractor shall fill out a separate
utility summary sheet for each dredging region. The Contractor shall
also submit a copy of all utility as-builts, surveys, etc., received
from the utility owner. All utility as-builts shall be labeled such
that each as-built has the current owner's name and pipeline location
(C/L Station and Mile #) on it;
d. All information shown on the contract plates and a record of all
completed work, including any deviations, modifications, or changes
from those plates, however minor, which may have been incorporated
into the work;
e. Neat line and actual quantity by reach of dredging;
f. All additional work not appearing on the contract plates; and
g. Each various feature of work performed shall be distinguishable by
color coding and/or symbology. As a minimum the following features
shall be depicted on the as-built drawings:
(1) Reaches of channel dredged, including gross and net yards, and
dates dredged.

areas) as verified by owners including station, C/L (or B/L)

XY-coordinate, minimum elevation, utility size, utility type, and

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit hard copies of all submittals unless waived by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit hard copies of all submittals unless waived by the CO.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall enter and update the contract project schedule in RMS by either manually entering all schedule data or by importing the Standard Data Exchange Format (SDEF) file.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter and update the project schedule in RMS manually or via SDEF import.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure that all closeout documents are entered, completed, and documented within RMS.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure all closeout documents are entered, completed, and documented in RMS.

rows.verbatim: Use of RMS as described in the preceding paragraphs is mandatory.
rows.normalized: Use of RMS as described is mandatory for the Contractor.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall ensure that sufficient resources are available to maintain contract data within the RMS system.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure sufficient resources to maintain contract data in RMS.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall take corrective action within 7 calendar days after receipt of notice of RMS non-compliance by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must take corrective action within 7 calendar days of receiving an RMS non-compliance notice.

rows.verbatim: In order to prevent, and to provide for abatement and control of any environmental pollution arising from construction activities in the performance of this contract, the Contractor and his/her subcontractors shall comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local laws, and regulations concerning environmental pollution control and abatement.
rows.normalized: Contractor and subcontractors must comply with all applicable Federal, State, and Local environmental pollution laws and regulations.

rows.verbatim: All costs for the work covered under this section shall be distributed throughout the existing bid items.
rows.normalized: Costs for environmental protection work must be distributed throughout existing bid items.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall establish and maintain a plan for environmental protection, to assure compliance with contract specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and maintain an environmental protection plan to assure compliance.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall also maintain records of environmental protection for all dredging operations, including but not limited to the following:
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain environmental protection records for dredging operations, including the listed items (continued on next page).

rows.verbatim: a. Environmental pollution control plan; b. Applicable Federal, State, and Local pollution control regulations; c. Air Pollution - dust, smoke, noise, etc.; d. Water Pollution - disposal of water, oil, etc.; e. Land Pollution - debris disposal, restoration of temporary construction sites, etc.; f. Training course for employees; g. Corrective actions taken.
rows.normalized: Required environmental protection records include: pollution control plan, applicable regulations, air pollution, water pollution, land pollution, training course, and corrective actions; 7 items total (continuation of list from prior page).

rows.verbatim: Within 120 hours after receiving notice to proceed, the Contractor shall submit, in writing, proposals for environmental pollution control, disposal of debris and trash, and an Environmental Protection Plan, and
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit written proposals for pollution control, debris/trash disposal, and an Environmental Protection Plan within 120 hours of NTP.

rows.verbatim: When directed by the Contracting Officer to a Secondary Dredging Region, the Contractor shall re-submit the endangered species portion of the Environmental Protection Plan applicable to that region.
rows.normalized: If directed to a Secondary Dredging Region, Contractor must re-submit the endangered species portion of the Environmental Protection Plan for that region.

rows.verbatim: No part of time lost due to such a stop order shall be made the subject of a claim for time extensions or for excess costs or damages by the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not claim time extensions or excess costs/damages for time lost due to a stop order.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be responsible for ensuring that all subcontractors comply with these environmental clauses.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for ensuring all subcontractors comply with environmental clauses.

rows.verbatim: Such notice, when delivered to the Contractor or the Contractor's authorized representative at the site of work, shall be deemed sufficient for this purpose.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: Such notice, when delivered to the Contractor or the Contractor's authorized representative at the site of work, shall be deemed sufficient for this purpose.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall inform the Government Inspector, Contracting Officer's Representative, and Administrative Contracting Officer, who will in turn contact CEMVN Historic Preservation (HP) staff.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inform the Government Inspector, COR, and ACO of discoveries.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall not proceed with work in the vicinity until CEMVN HP staff completes consultation with the State Historic Preservation Offices and others unless notified otherwise.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not proceed with work in the vicinity until CEMVN HP staff completes consultation, unless notified otherwise.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall not pollute any body of water with fuels; oils; bitumens; calcium chlorides; herbicides; insecticides; other materials harmful to fish, shellfish, or wildlife; or with materials that may be a detriment to outdoor recreation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not pollute any body of water with listed harmful materials.

rows.verbatim: The redistribution or reinjection of pollutants pre-existing in dredged material or river water will not be considered as pollution caused by the Contractor.
rows.normalized: Pre-existing pollutants redistributed or reinjected during dredging are not considered Contractor-caused pollution.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall assist the Government, using available on-site plant and manpower, in monitoring the water quality aspects of the dredging and disposal operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must assist the Government, using on-site plant and manpower, in monitoring water quality during dredging/disposal.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall keep construction activities under surveillance, management, and control to minimize interference with, disturbance to, and damage of fish and wildlife.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep construction activities under surveillance/control to minimize harm to fish and wildlife.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall not alter natural water flows or otherwise disturb natural habitat adjacent to or within the project area that are critical to fish or wildlife.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not alter natural water flows or disturb critical habitat.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall instruct all personnel associated with the project of the potential presence of manatees in the area, and the need to avoid collisions with these animals.
rows.normalized: Contractor must instruct all project personnel about potential manatee presence and need to avoid collisions.

rows.verbatim: All construction personnel shall be advised that there are civil and criminal penalties for harming, harassing, or killing manatees.
rows.normalized: All construction personnel must be advised of civil/criminal penalties for harming manatees.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall be held responsible for any manatee harmed, harassed, or killed as a result of construction activities not conducted in accordance with these specifications.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for manatees harmed/killed due to non-compliant construction activities.

rows.verbatim: Prior to commencement of construction, each vessel involved in construction activities shall display at the vessel control station or in a prominent location, visible to all employees operating the vessel, a temporary sign at least 8-1/2 inches by 11 inches reading, "CAUTION: MANATEE HABITAT/IDLE SPEED IS REQUIRED IN CONSTRUCTION AREA."
rows.normalized: Prior to construction, each vessel must display a manatee caution sign of specified size at the control station or prominent visible location.

rows.verbatim: In the absence of a vessel, a temporary three foot by four foot sign reading "CAUTION: MANATEE AREA" shall be posted adjacent to the issued construction permit.
rows.normalized: If no vessel is used, a 3x4 foot manatee caution sign must be posted adjacent to the construction permit.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall remove the signs upon completion of construction.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: The Contractor shall remove the signs upon completion of construction.

rows.verbatim:
(1) If a manatee(s) is sighted within 100 yards of the project
area, all appropriate precautions shall be implemented by the
Contractor to ensure protection of the manatee.
rows.normalized: If a manatee is sighted within 100 yards of the project area, Contractor must implement all appropriate precautions to protect the manatee.

rows.verbatim: These precautions shall include the operation of all moving equipment no closer than 50 feet of a manatee.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: These precautions shall include the operation of all moving equipment no closer than 50 feet of a manatee.

rows.verbatim: If a manatee is closer than 50 feet to moving equipment or the project area, the equipment shall be shut down and all construction activities shall cease to ensure protection of the manatee.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: If a manatee is closer than 50 feet to moving equipment or the project area, the equipment shall be shut down and all construction activities shall cease to ensure protection of the manatee.

rows.verbatim: Construction activities shall not resume until the manatee has departed and the 50-foot buffer has been reestablished.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: Construction activities shall not resume until the manatee has departed and the 50-foot buffer has been reestablished.

rows.verbatim:
(2) If a manatee(s) is sighted in the project area, all vessels
associated with the project shall operate at "no wake/idle" speeds
at all times, and vessels will follow routes of deep water
whenever possible, until the manatee has departed the project
area.
rows.normalized: If a manatee is sighted in the project area, all project vessels must operate at no wake/idle speeds and follow deep water routes until the manatee departs.

rows.verbatim: Boats used to transport personnel shall be shallow-draft vessels, preferably of the light-displacement category, where navigational safety permits.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: Boats used to transport personnel shall be shallow-draft vessels, preferably of the light-displacement category, where navigational safety permits.

rows.verbatim:
(3) If siltation barriers are used, they shall be made of
material in which manatees cannot become entangled, are properly
secured, and are regularly monitored to avoid manatee entrapment.
rows.normalized: If siltation barriers are used, they must be made of non-entangling material, properly secured, and regularly monitored to avoid manatee entrapment.

rows.verbatim: Any sightings of manatees or collisions with a manatee shall be immediately reported to the Corps of Engineers.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: Any sightings of manatees or collisions with a manatee shall be immediately reported to the Corps of Engineers.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall ensure that the following are done to reduce the
likelihood of Sturgeon entrainment:
a. When lowering the ladder, the pumping rate should be reduced to
the lowest speed feasible while the cutterhead is being lowered.
b. The cutterhead remains completely buried in the channel bottom
during dredging operations.
c. If pumping water through the cutterhead is deemed necessary to
dislodge material, or to clean the pumps, the pumping rate should be
reduced to the lowest rate feasible while raising the ladder until the
cutterhead is at least at mid-depth at which point the pumping rate
can be increased.
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure the following measures (a-c) are done to reduce likelihood of Sturgeon entrainment; 3 items in total.

rows.verbatim:
a. The Contractor shall provide daily trash collection and cleanup of
the dredge and attendant plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide daily trash collection and cleanup of the dredge and attendant plant.

rows.verbatim: Disposal locations for waste materials, effluents, trash, garbage, oil, grease, chemicals, etc., shall be such that harmful debris will
rows.normalized: Contractor must ensure disposal locations for waste materials are such that harmful debris will not escape into protected areas (sentence continues across page marker).

rows.verbatim: not enter the waterway, adjacent wetlands, or the disposal areas;
rows.normalized: Continuation: harmful debris must not enter the waterway, adjacent wetlands, or the disposal areas.

rows.verbatim:
prevent the use of the area for recreation; or present a hazard to
wildlife. Debris disposal shall be in accordance with applicable
Federal, State, and Local regulations, and shall be performed in a
manner approved by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Disposal must not prevent recreational use or hazard wildlife; debris disposal must comply with applicable regulations and be performed in a manner approved by the Contracting Officer (continuation from prior page).

rows.verbatim:
During the life of this contract, the Contractor shall maintain all
facilities constructed for pollution control for as long as the operations
creating the particular pollutant are being carried out, or until the
material concerned has become stabilized to the extent that pollution is
no longer being created.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain all pollution control facilities for the life of the contract until pollution ceases or stabilizes.

rows.verbatim:
Early in the contract period the Contractor
shall conduct a training course that will emphasize all phases of
environmental protection.
rows.normalized: Contractor must conduct an environmental protection training course early in the contract period.

rows.verbatim:
This course shall involve all Contractor
personnel working on the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have all contract personnel attend/participate in the environmental training course.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall notify the
Contracting Officer of the scheduled time for this course so that the
Contracting Officer's Representative can attend.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify the Contracting Officer of the training course schedule so the COR can attend.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall remove all debris caused by the use of polystyrene
(styrofoam or similar material) floating pipelines, at the dredge site or
any other locations used to install, store, or repair the floating
pipeline.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove all debris caused by polystyrene floating pipeline use at the dredge site or related locations.

rows.verbatim:
Suitable banding, mesh, or other covering shall be placed on
the polystyrene floating pipeline to prevent deterioration during normal
dredging operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must place suitable banding, mesh, or covering on polystyrene floating pipeline to prevent deterioration.

rows.verbatim:
The discharge pipeline shall conform to
lighting requirements set forth by the US Coast Guard in the "Rules of the
Road, International-Inland" https://www.navcen.uscg.gov/pdf/navrules/navrules.
pdf.
rows.normalized: Contractor's discharge pipeline must conform to US Coast Guard lighting requirements per the Rules of the Road.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall furnish daily janitorial services for the dredge and
attendant plant during the entire life of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish daily janitorial services for the dredge and plant for the life of the contract.

rows.verbatim:
The bathroom
facilities shall be kept clean and sanitary at all times.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep bathroom facilities clean and sanitary at all times.

rows.verbatim:
Services shall be performed at such a time and in such a
manner to least interfere with operations, and need only be accomplished
when the facilities are in daily use.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform janitorial services at times/manner that least interfere with operations, only when facilities are in daily use.

rows.verbatim:
If an oil spill or chemical release occurs during the performance of this
contract, the Contractor shall contact the National Response Center at
1-800-424-8802, as soon as possible.
rows.normalized: If an oil spill or chemical release occurs, Contractor must contact the National Response Center as soon as possible.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall comply with the
instructions from the responding agency concerning containment and cleanup of
the spill, and
shall provide the Contracting Officer with a complete written report of
the incident.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with the responding agency's instructions on containment/cleanup and must provide the Contracting Officer a complete written report of the incident.

rows.verbatim:
Facilities for the
storage, preparation, and serving of food will likewise be kept clean and
sanitary.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep food storage, preparation, and serving facilities clean and sanitary.

rows.verbatim: Unless otherwise specified, surveys and surveying shall be in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, Engineering and Design, Hydrographic Surveying, latest edition.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform surveys and surveying in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, latest edition, unless otherwise specified.

rows.verbatim: All costs for the work covered under this section shall be included in the contract unit price per hour in the applicable "Dredging" and "Option Dredging" items on the bidding schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include all costs for this section's work in the contract unit price per hour under the Dredging and Option Dredging bid items.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall establish and maintain quality control for the work specified in this section to assure compliance with the contract requirements and maintain records of his quality control for all surveying including but not limited to the following:
a. Layouts and Surveys. Daily log of layout work and surveys
consisting of type and location using the Government established
baselines and gages as stated in the Contract Clause entitled "Layout
of Work" (FAR 52.236-17).
b. Reporting. The original and two copies of these reports and tests
as well as the records of corrective action taken, shall be furnished
daily to the Government. The report shall include a record of times
and dates surveys were run, the horizontal control stations used and
their coordinates, the vertical control points used and their
elevations, and weather conditions.
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish and maintain quality control records for surveying, including at minimum (a) daily layout/survey logs and (b) daily reports with specified contents furnished to the Government.

rows.verbatim: All surveys shall be performed in the presence of the Government Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform all surveys in the presence of the Government Representative.

rows.verbatim: All surveys shall be performed under the direction of and certified by a Professional Land Surveyor currently licensed by any state in the United States of America.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have all surveys performed under the direction of, and certified by, a Professional Land Surveyor licensed in a U.S. state.

rows.verbatim: In addition, the surveyor shall document at least three years of experience in hydrographic surveying of navigable channels.
rows.normalized: The surveyor must document at least three years of experience in hydrographic surveying of navigable channels.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit, to the Contracting Officer for review, a plan for the verification of surveying equipment described herein.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit a surveying equipment verification plan to the Contracting Officer for review.

rows.verbatim: The plan shall include types, certifications, calibration checks, etc., for the surveying equipment.
rows.normalized: The verification plan must include equipment types, certifications, and calibration checks, etc.

rows.verbatim:
a. The Contractor shall furnish survey vessel(s), diesel or gasoline
powered, twin engine, not less than 30 feet in length, and equipped
with the following:
- Enclosed cabin;
- Space for four (4) passengers;
- Heating/air conditioning;
- Fully operated;
- U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) certified;
- Navigation radar, as described in Section 35 20 23.23, paragraph
entitled "Navigation Radar";
- Operable radio (same frequency as the dredge) for each dredge in
operation;
- A surveying lead line as described in EM 1110-2-1003, Appendix B-2.
- Hydrographic Surveying System: Hydrographic surveying software
(HYPACK or equivalent) and electronic horizontal positioning
(Differentially corrected Global Positioning, DGPS), depth sounding
and data acquisition instrumentation. The use of motion compensation
(a heave/pitch/roll sensor) is optional; however, if it is not used,
then the conduct of the survey will be restricted by roll/pitch/heave
sea-state limits [>10 degrees (roll-pitch), >.5 foot (heave)] as
interpreted by the on-site Government Representative. Additionally,
if the survey system utilizes motion compensation, then a side, bow or
stern mounting of the fathometer transducer is acceptable; however, if
motion compensation is not available, then the transducer must be hull
mounted.
- The vessel(s) must, at minimum, have a fathometer bar check
apparatus as described in EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-10.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish survey vessel(s) meeting minimum size/power specs and equipped with the listed items, including enclosed cabin, passenger space, HVAC, USCG certification, navigation radar, radio, lead line, hydrographic surveying system (with conditional motion-compensation/mounting rules), and a fathometer bar check apparatus.

rows.verbatim:
The height of the fathometer transducer face while the vessel(s)
is static (draft) and in motion (settlement, squat) must be determined
as described in EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-13.
rows.normalized: Contractor must determine the fathometer transducer face height while the vessel is static and in motion, per EM 1110-2-1003 para 4-13.

rows.verbatim:
A method must be
established to determine and correct for any vessel draft changes
during the surveying period [ex: Real-Time Kinematic (RTK)
observations at static draft to increasing engine RPM (paragraph
4-13c)].
rows.normalized: Contractor must establish a method to determine and correct for vessel draft changes during surveying.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to surveying operations, a hydrographic system latency bias
calibration test must be performed and the latency correctors must be
applied (EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-15).
rows.normalized: Before surveying operations, Contractor must perform a hydrographic system latency bias calibration test and apply latency correctors.

rows.verbatim:
"No Smoking" signs shall be posted and no smoking will be allowed
when occupied by Government personnel.
rows.normalized: Contractor must post "No Smoking" signs and prohibit smoking when Government personnel are aboard.

rows.verbatim:
The acoustic ping rate shall be, at minimum, 10
soundings per second.
rows.normalized: The fathometer's acoustic ping rate must be at least 10 soundings per second.

rows.verbatim:
To limit signal attenuation in areas of
unconsolidated bottom sediments, the acoustic frequency utilized shall be
within the range of 24-28 KHz and the Low Frequency Low Pulse Width shall
be in accordance with the Manufacturers recommended settings for
unconsolidated bottom sediments in shallow water depths (i.e., 0 to 150
feet).
rows.normalized: The acoustic frequency used must be within 24-28 KHz and the Low Frequency Low Pulse Width must follow manufacturer settings for unconsolidated bottom sediments in shallow water (0-150 ft).

rows.verbatim:
If a dual frequency fathometer is utilized, then the low frequency
shall be within the 24-28 KHz range.
rows.normalized: If a dual frequency fathometer is used, the low frequency must be within 24-28 KHz.

rows.verbatim:
At minimum, the equipment shall be
capable of recording depths of water ranging from three feet under the
transducer face(s) to a maximum of 50 feet.
rows.normalized: The equipment must be capable of recording water depths from 3 feet under the transducer face to a maximum of 50 feet.

rows.verbatim:
At this maximum depth, the
sounding accuracy must be 0.5 feet (28 KHz transducer).
rows.normalized: At the maximum depth, sounding accuracy must be 0.5 feet using a 28 KHz transducer.

rows.verbatim:
Acoustic returns
shall be recorded on thermal chart paper by a fixed, high-resolution
printing element (no stylus).
rows.normalized: Acoustic returns must be recorded on thermal chart paper using a fixed, high-resolution printing element (no stylus).

rows.verbatim:
A digital fathometer may be used instead of
paper charts as directed by the Contracting Officer's Representative, but
the Contractor must still be capable of producing paper charts unless
otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: If a digital fathometer is used instead of paper charts, the Contractor must still be able to produce paper charts unless otherwise directed.

rows.verbatim:
The paper
chart scaling shall be in English units, no greater than 0-50 feet
full-scale and graduated in 1 foot increments with numeric depth
annotations at the 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 foot chart levels.
rows.normalized: Paper chart scaling must be in English units, no greater than 0-50 feet full scale, graduated in 1-foot increments with depth annotations at 0,10,20,30,40,50 feet.

rows.verbatim:
The
instrument shall, at minimum, be capable of adjusting transmit power,
receiver sensitivity and time-varied gain settings and of inputting the
correct speed-of-sound, vessel draft and tide values.
rows.normalized: The fathometer must be capable of adjusting transmit power, receiver sensitivity, time-varied gain, and inputting speed-of-sound, draft, and tide values.

rows.verbatim:
Additionally, the
surveyor shall print the control parameter settings on the chart paper at
the start of all surveys and when any control settings are changed and
before and after all bar checks.
rows.normalized: The surveyor must print control parameter settings on the chart paper at the start of surveys, when settings change, and before/after bar checks.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to the Contractor taking
preliminary field surveys, control parameter settings shall be turned into
the Government Inspector for review to ensure the settings meet the
surveying parameters.
rows.normalized: Before taking preliminary field surveys, Contractor must submit control parameter settings to the Government Inspector for review.

rows.verbatim:
During the surveying of run lines, the fathometer
shall be capable of annotating periodic event marks on the paper chart as
directed by other surveying system components (positioning, controlling
software) and be capable of transmitting each event sounding back to these
system components for horizontal position tagging and data storage.
rows.normalized: During run-line surveying, the fathometer must be capable of annotating event marks and transmitting event soundings for position tagging and data storage.

rows.verbatim:
Hydrographic fathometer calibrations shall be performed at the survey site
by methods described in EM 1110-2-1003, paragraphs 4-10 through 4-15 and
at a frequency listed in table 4-6 for navigation and dredging support
surveys with soft bottom materials.
rows.normalized: Contractor must perform fathometer calibrations at the survey site per EM 1110-2-1003 paras 4-10 to 4-15 at the frequency in table 4-6.

rows.verbatim:
The acoustic traces of the bar or ball check calibrations shall be captured
on the fathometer paper chart (at the 10, 20, and 30 foot depths, or as
directed by the Government Representative) along with a notation
indicating the site location (i.e., station, lat/long, x, y), the date and
time.
rows.normalized: Acoustic traces of bar/ball check calibrations must be captured on the paper chart with site location, date, and time notations.

rows.verbatim:
Additionally, if a velocity
meter probe is utilized, the average speed-of-sound reading for the entire
water column and the location, date and time of the probe sounding must
also be noted on the fathometer paper chart.
rows.normalized: If a velocity meter probe is used, the average speed-of-sound reading and probe sounding location/date/time must also be noted on the paper chart.

rows.verbatim:
All calibration
and soundings shall be made in the presence and to the satisfaction of the
Government Representative at the job site.
rows.normalized: All calibration and soundings must be made in the presence and to the satisfaction of the Government Representative at the job site.

rows.verbatim:
The Low Frequency Pulse Width range of cycles (i.e., 1 to 10) used shall
not produce signal lengths less than 35 microseconds or greater than 125
microseconds.
rows.normalized: The Low Frequency Pulse Width setting used must not produce signal lengths shorter than 35 microseconds or longer than 125 microseconds.

rows.verbatim:
The hydrographic surveying vessel(s) must meet or exceed horizontal
accuracy of U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) Maritime Differential Global
Positioning System (DGPS) instrumentation for determining horizontal
positioning during surveying operations in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003,
paragraph 7-3.
rows.normalized: Contractor's hydrographic surveying vessel(s) must meet or exceed USCG DGPS horizontal accuracy standards per EM 1110-2-1003 para 7-3.

rows.verbatim:
This DGPS instrumentation must have a positioning accuracy
of 1-3 meters 2DRMS.
rows.normalized: Contractor's DGPS instrumentation must have 1-3 meter 2DRMS positioning accuracy.

rows.verbatim:
If the USCG system is to be utilized, then
the English Turn beacon site shall be the source for differential
corrections.
rows.normalized: If the Contractor utilizes the USCG system, the English Turn beacon site shall be the source for differential corrections.

rows.verbatim:
The GPS antenna on the survey vessel(s) must be physically
positioned directly above the fathometer transducer or the hydrographic
surveying software suite must be capable of aligning the horizontal and
vertical sensors.
rows.normalized: Contractor's GPS antenna must be positioned above the fathometer transducer, or the survey software must be able to align horizontal and vertical sensors.

rows.verbatim:
The hydrographic surveying vessel(s) must reduce final survey
elevations relative to project datum using tide staffs referenced in the
Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor's survey vessel(s) must reduce final survey elevations relative to project datum using referenced tide staffs.

rows.verbatim:
As directed by the Contracting Officer's
Representative, visual water level observations, Real-Time Kinematic
(RTK), Real-Time Networks (RTN), or post-processed kinematic elevation
computations shall be used in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003, paragraphs
7-11 through 7-14.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall use visual water level observations, RTK, RTN, or post-processed kinematic computations as directed, per EM 1110-2-1003 paragraphs 7-11 through 7-14.

rows.verbatim:
Real-time or post-processed methods must include a
static observation adjacent to the tide staff(s) for calibration of
orthometric heights to project datum.
rows.normalized: Real-time or post-processed methods must include a static observation adjacent to tide staffs for calibration.

rows.verbatim:
Surveys for all fixed stations shall be performed in accordance with EM
1110-2-1003, Chapter 4 - Section IV "Data Collection, Editing, and
Processing".
rows.normalized: Contractor shall perform surveys for all fixed stations in accordance with EM 1110-2-1003 Chapter 4 Section IV.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall be able to use this data to lay out the work and
subsequently provide completed work as specified herein to the
Government.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall be able to use the provided survey data to lay out the work and provide completed work as specified.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to initiating positioning surveys using electronic survey
equipment, a calibration test of the electronic measuring device
shall be performed according to the manufacturer's instructions in the
presence of the Contracting Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Prior to initiating positioning surveys, a calibration test of the electronic measuring device shall be performed per manufacturer's instructions in the presence of the COR.

rows.verbatim:
Calibration checks
shall be run at the beginning and completion of each day's survey or
portion thereof.
rows.normalized: Calibration checks shall be run at the beginning and completion of each day's survey or portion thereof.

rows.verbatim:
Results shall be furnished daily to the Contracting
Officer's Representative.
rows.normalized: Results shall be furnished daily to the Contracting Officer's Representative.

rows.verbatim:
All electronic surveys
shall be tied to a fixed station.
rows.normalized: All electronic surveys shall be tied to a fixed station.

rows.verbatim:
Should the electronic measuring device fail to
indicate the known distance within the factory defined error range for the
device, the device shall not be used for determining survey positions.
rows.normalized: If the electronic measuring device fails to indicate the known distance within the factory-defined error range, the device shall not be used for determining survey positions.

rows.verbatim: Surveys will include but will not be limited to the following surveys.
rows.normalized: The Contractor's surveys will include, but not be limited to, the surveys described in the following subsections.

rows.verbatim:
Prior to taking any original cross sections, the Contractor shall run a
preliminary field survey electronically controlled locating the
baseline/centerline, towers, all buoys, channel markers, utility
crossings, P.C.'s, P.T.'s, P.I.'s, and P.O.T.'s within the limits of the
survey area.
rows.normalized: Prior to taking original cross sections, the Contractor shall run a preliminary field survey locating specified features within the survey area.

rows.verbatim:
The data from this survey
shall be plotted on a plan sheet and submitted to the Contracting Officer
for confirmation of correct channel alignment.
rows.normalized: The preliminary survey data shall be plotted on a plan sheet and submitted to the Contracting Officer for alignment confirmation.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall also submit a Hypack Channel file
(.chn) that depicts the channel alignment of the entire dredging region
prior to the pre-construction conference.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall submit a Hypack Channel file depicting the channel alignment prior to the pre-construction conference.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall not
proceed with any dredging work until the Contracting Officer determines
the final channel alignment and furnishes this information to the
Contractor.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall not proceed with dredging work until the Contracting Officer determines and furnishes the final channel alignment.

rows.verbatim:
Depth soundings shall be made with the
hydrographic surveying system (as described in the paragraph entitled
"Survey Equipment") and the recorded sounding resolution shall be one
sounding for every 5 feet along the cross section runlines (normal to
the centerline).
rows.normalized: Depth soundings shall be made with the hydrographic surveying system at one sounding per 5 feet along cross section runlines.

rows.verbatim:
The recorded depths shall be to a resolution of 0.1
feet.
rows.normalized: Recorded depths shall be to a resolution of 0.1 feet.

rows.verbatim:
The sensitivity/gain control setting that is selected for the
survey area bottom material-type must also be used for the bar check
calibrations and must not be adjusted during hydrographic surveying
(EM 1110-2-1003, paragraph 4-6).
rows.normalized: The selected sensitivity/gain control setting must also be used for bar check calibrations and must not be adjusted during surveying.

rows.verbatim:
In areas of consolidated bottom
material, the digitized and recorded depth soundings shall indicate
the true channel bottom.
rows.normalized: In areas of consolidated bottom material, digitized and recorded depth soundings shall indicate the true channel bottom.

rows.verbatim:
However, in survey areas containing
unconsolidated bottom materials, acoustic measurements must be
calibrated with lead line measurements.
rows.normalized: In survey areas with unconsolidated bottom materials, acoustic measurements must be calibrated with lead line measurements.

rows.verbatim:
These leadline measurements
must be notated on the fathometer paper chart and taken at a minimum
of 5,000 foot intervals; on the channel centerline and both edges of
cut, or as determined by the Government Representative on the
jobsite.
rows.normalized: Leadline measurements must be notated on the fathometer paper chart and taken at a minimum of 5,000 foot intervals on centerline and cut edges.

rows.verbatim:
The real-time
fathometer paper charting of the surveying runs, to include calibration
and leadline events and all survey notations, shall be furnished to the
Government.
rows.normalized: Real-time fathometer paper charting including calibration and leadline events shall be furnished to the Government.

rows.verbatim:
Stored
hydrographic data (x,y,z) shall also be furnished to the Government in
a structured ASCII format on compact disk (CD) media.
rows.normalized: Stored hydrographic data shall also be furnished to the Government in structured ASCII format on CD media.

rows.verbatim:
A chart layout of the before dredging cross sections shall be
prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Contracting Officer's
Representative.
rows.normalized: A chart layout of the before dredging cross sections shall be prepared by the Contractor and approved by the COR.

rows.verbatim:
This graphical chart must represent a scaled plan
view of the survey area with the recorded 5 foot interval depth
soundings (0.1 foot resolution) plotted at their x,y positions.
rows.normalized: The graphical chart must represent a scaled plan view with 5-foot interval depth soundings plotted at x,y positions.

rows.verbatim: The actual location of each sounding taken on each before dredging cross section range shall be provided.
rows.normalized: Found by the coverage check and not by the reader: The actual location of each sounding taken on each before dredging cross section range shall be provided.

rows.verbatim:
Soundings shall be to the nearest 0.1-foot referred to the
water surface.
rows.normalized: Soundings shall be to the nearest 0.1-foot referred to the water surface.

rows.verbatim:
This information shall also be plotted on a printout sheet, horizontal vertical scale, along with a section showing the
required dredging dimensions.
rows.normalized: The sounding information shall also be plotted on a printout sheet with a section showing required dredging dimensions.

rows.verbatim:
The time and date taken shall be shown
and the gage reading applicable to the survey shall be shown.
rows.normalized: The time and date taken shall be shown, and the applicable gage reading shall be shown.

rows.verbatim:
The
applicable gage shall be read to the nearest 0.1-foot prior to and
after each day's survey.
rows.normalized: The applicable gage shall be read to the nearest 0.1-foot before and after each day's survey.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall
remove, at no additional cost to the
Government, any material in the navigation channel outside the area
designated to be dredged if the material falls within the channel and
was not indicated on the before dredging survey (roll effect downstream
of the cutterhead dredge).
rows.normalized: If material falls in the channel and was not indicated on the before dredging survey, the Contractor shall remove it at no additional cost.

rows.verbatim:
The data obtained from the electronic positioning/control system and the
fathometer shall be collected, recorded, and processed.
rows.normalized: Data from electronic positioning/control system and fathometer shall be collected, recorded, and processed.

rows.verbatim:
Soundings shall
be recorded to the nearest 0.1-foot and the X and Y coordinates of these
soundings shall be recorded to the nearest foot.
rows.normalized: Soundings shall be recorded to nearest 0.1-foot and X/Y coordinates to nearest foot.

rows.verbatim:
More
frequent readings will be required when directed by the Government
Inspector.
rows.normalized: More frequent readings will be required of the Contractor when directed by the Government Inspector.

rows.verbatim:
From the processed data, the Contractor shall
provide certain survey information taken for the purpose of computing the
total amount of work to be paid for.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall provide certain survey information from processed data for computing total work to be paid.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor must furnish the
required data on CD/DVD/e-mail containing ASCII character set.
rows.normalized: The Contractor must furnish required data on CD/DVD/e-mail in ASCII character set.

rows.verbatim:
The information received shall be free of errors and in the
following format:
(a) the X-coordinate in feet of a recognized Louisiana Lambert grid
system, (b) the Y-coordinate in feet of same recognized Louisiana grid
system, (c) the elevation, and (d) remarks such as the station number
(i.e. 1+00), CL (for centerline), ES (for end of station), EJ (end of
file), and direction of survey (either "L" for + or "R" for -, followed by
Station No., i.e. L 30+00).
rows.normalized: Submitted data shall be free of errors and formatted with X-coordinate, Y-coordinate, elevation, and remarks as specified; 4 format elements in total.

rows.verbatim:
The time and date the cross section was taken
and the gage reading applicable to the section must be included.
rows.normalized: The time/date of the cross section and applicable gage reading must be included.

rows.verbatim:
The
electronically recorded data files, along with a hard copy of the track
plotter surveys, plotted on the chart to show compliance with alignment,
and quantity computations shall be presented to the Government
Representative on site no later than three days after the survey is
taken.
rows.normalized: Electronically recorded data files, hard copy track plotter surveys, and quantity computations shall be presented to the Government Representative no later than three days after the survey.

rows.verbatim:
Not submitting the data in accordance to the specifications and
within the allotted time will be cause to withhold progress payment.
rows.normalized: Failure to submit data per specifications and within the allotted time will cause withholding of progress payment.

rows.verbatim:
Under no circumstances
shall the information be edited for the purpose of eliminating incorrect
soundings.
rows.normalized: Under no circumstances shall the information be edited to eliminate incorrect soundings.

The Contractor shall provide a separate file listing all incorrect
soundings to be eliminated.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall provide a separate file listing all incorrect soundings to be eliminated.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall

unless otherwise directed by the Government Inspector.
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall submit a separate survey file for each 2,000 feet acceptance reach unless otherwise directed by the Government Inspector.

rows.verbatim:

previous file (i.e., Sta. 820+00 to 840+00, Sta. 840+00 to 860+00, etc.).
rows.normalized: The beginning station for each file shall be the repeated ending station from the previous file.

rows.verbatim:
Upon completion of dredging in a designated reach, waterway profiles shall
be taken over the same dredging reach.
rows.normalized: Upon completion of dredging in a designated reach, waterway profiles shall be taken over that reach.

rows.verbatim:
Distances between soundings on
each profile shall be 20 feet.
rows.normalized: Distances between soundings on each profile shall be 20 feet.

rows.verbatim:
Controlled profiles of the waterway shall
be made along the dredge cut centerline and one at each outside bottom
edge of the cut.
rows.normalized: Controlled profiles of the waterway shall be made along the dredge cut centerline and at each outside bottom edge of the cut.

This information shall be plotted

rows.normalized: Profile information shall be plotted on a printout sheet at specified horizontal and vertical scales.

rows.verbatim:

measured by the cubic yard by computing the volume along the centerline

Tolerances".

Sections".
rows.normalized: The Contractor shall make dredging volume computations and furnish them to the Government with before/after survey data.

C/L with an interpolated elevation.

rows.verbatim:
The dredge plant length measured horizontally from the digging
spud to the cutterhead's location while dredging at a channel depth of
67 feet, measured from the water surface, shall be no less than 262
feet to meet the swing requirements specified in subparagraph (c).
rows.normalized: Dredge plant length from digging spud to cutterhead must be no less than 262 feet at 67-foot channel depth.

rows.verbatim:
Dredges shall meet or exceed the minimum production rate
requirements listed in the table located in the Dredging Region
Section(s).
rows.normalized: Dredges must meet or exceed minimum production rate requirements in the Dredging Region Section tables.

rows.verbatim:
b. Submerged pumps shall meet the following conditions in order for
the dredge to be classified as utilizing a submerged pump:
(1) The submerged pump shall be located on the cutterhead ladder
and shall be placed at a distance of no more than two-thirds the
length of the ladder from the cutterhead.
(2) The submerged pump shall be fully immersed.
(3) The submerged pump is operating.
rows.normalized: Submerged pumps must meet all listed conditions (location on ladder/placement, full immersion, operation) to be classified as utilizing a submerged pump; 3 conditions total.

rows.verbatim:
c. The cutterhead ladder shall be of sufficient length to provide a
uniformly dredged channel depth of 67 feet, measured from the water
surface.
rows.normalized: The cutterhead ladder must be of sufficient length to provide a uniformly dredged channel depth of 67 feet.

rows.verbatim:
The spuds shall be of sufficient length to perform dredging
operations in water depths from 11 to 70 feet.
rows.normalized: Spuds must be of sufficient length to perform dredging operations in water depths from 11 to 70 feet.

rows.verbatim:
The dredge shall be
capable, from each setting of the spud, of dredging a channel at least
300 foot wide, while swinging through an arc of 35 degrees to either
side of the centerline of the cut (total arc 70 degrees or less) while
at a depth of 67 feet, measured from the water surface.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be capable of dredging a channel at least 300 feet wide through a 70-degree total swing arc at 67-foot depth, from each spud setting.

rows.verbatim:
The
Contractor shall fulfill the requirements of this subparagraph and
subparagraph (a) while achieving or exceeding the minimum production
rate requirements listed in the tables at the end of the applicable
Dredging Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must fulfill the swing/length requirements while achieving or exceeding minimum production rate requirements in the Dredging Region Section tables.

rows.verbatim:
d. The Contractor shall have available for use at all times a variety
of interchangeable pump impellers to permit the dredge to operate
under the varying conditions described in the applicable Dredging
Region Section(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must have available at all times a variety of interchangeable pump impellers.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor shall also have
available replacement blades and knives for the dredge pump and wipers
for the cutter.
rows.normalized: Contractor must have available replacement blades, knives for the dredge pump, and wipers for the cutter.

rows.verbatim:

pump functions and a pump engine recording tachometer.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with recording vacuum/pressure gauges, an electronic data printout, and a pump engine recording tachometer.

rows.verbatim:

rows.normalized: During dredging, instruments must record pipeline pressure, pump vacuum, and pump RPM data on control chart paper.

rows.verbatim:

rows.normalized: Contractor must deliver completed recordings to the Inspector on watch at time of removal, each day of operation.

rows.verbatim: f. The dredge shall be equipped with a gyro compass.
rows.normalized: The dredge must be equipped with a gyro compass.

Coast Guard Auxiliary and EM 385-1-1.

paragraph entitled "Global Positioning System (GPS) Equipment".

rows.normalized: Dredged material shall be placed between jetties and existing marsh, stacked not to exceed the west jetty elevation (+1.0 feet MLLW).

rows.normalized: Access to the disposal area shall be across existing jetties and/or via Breton Sound.

rows.normalized: Contractor shall take precautions during disposal operations to prevent damage to rock jetties and wetlands.

rows.verbatim: At no time shall dredge effluent material be allowed to exceed one foot in height over existing vegetated wetlands.
rows.normalized: Dredge effluent material shall not exceed one foot in height over existing vegetated wetlands at any time.

rows.verbatim: Nesting birds and their nests are protected by the Migratory Bird Treaty Act (MBTA) and must not be disturbed or destroyed.
rows.normalized: Nesting birds and their nests must not be disturbed or destroyed by the Contractor's work.

rows.verbatim: Protection within the project area shall be accomplished by the following: disturbance to deter nesting activity of coastal birds and wading birds prior to nesting; avoidance of active coastal bird, wading bird and pelican nesting areas; and avoidance of known eagle nests.
rows.normalized: Contractor must accomplish bird protection via: deterrence disturbance before nesting, avoidance of active nesting areas, and avoidance of known eagle nests.

rows.verbatim: Nest prevention and/or avoidance measures shall be required if nesting activity is observed during these times by the Contractor and verified by the Government.
rows.normalized: If nesting activity is observed during nesting periods and verified by Government, Contractor must implement nest prevention/avoidance measures.

rows.verbatim: These indicators of breeding activity shall be brought to the attention of the Government upon discovery to determine if nest prevention measures or avoidance measures are required.
rows.normalized: Contractor must bring coastal bird breeding indicators to Government's attention upon discovery.

rows.verbatim: The presence of eagles on and near these nesting sites should be reported to the Government and avoidance measures shall be implemented upon discovery.
rows.normalized: Avoidance measures must be implemented upon discovery of eagle nesting sites; presence should be reported to Government.

rows.verbatim: In addition to the requirements in Section 01 57 20.00 10, paragraph entitled "Implementation and Reporting", the Contractor shall also submit the Bird Nesting Prevention Plan.
rows.normalized: Contractor must also submit the Bird Nesting Prevention Plan.

rows.verbatim: The presence of coastal birds, wading birds, pelicans, and/or eagles exhibiting breeding behavior (as described in paragraph entitled "General") within the minimum distances from the work area (as specified in paragraph entitled "No Work Distances") shall be immediately reported to the Administrative Contracting Officer and to Jeff Corbino of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers at (504) 862-1958.
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately report breeding bird presence within minimum distances to the ACO and Jeff Corbino.
Contractor must observe no-work distances: coastal birds 650 ft, wading birds 1000 ft, pelicans 2000 ft, eagles 660 ft.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall prepare and submit, for approval, a plan detailing the efforts that will be undertaken to prevent birds from nesting within the minimum distances, as specified in the paragraph entitled "No Work Distances", from any work activity.
rows.normalized: Contractor must prepare and submit for approval a bird nest prevention plan.

rows.verbatim: This plan shall be submitted electronically to the Administrative Contracting Officer, the Contracting Officer's Representative, and to Mr. Jeff Corbino at Jeffrey.M.Corbino@usace.army.mil.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit the plan electronically to the ACO, COR, and Mr. Jeff Corbino.

rows.verbatim: Nest prevention measures shall be intended to deter birds from nesting on the disposal area(s) and access corridor(s) without physically harming birds during the nesting activity period.
rows.normalized: Nest prevention measures must deter nesting without physically harming birds.

rows.verbatim: The use of any harassment measures shall be in accordance with EM 385-1-1.
rows.normalized: Any harassment measures must comply with EM 385-1-1.

rows.verbatim:
At minimum, nest prevention measures shall include the following:
Flagging/Streamers - Flagging and/or streamers at least two feet in
length and which consist of reflective plastic/mylar type material
shall be attached to the top of stakes at least three feet in height.
The stakes shall be driven into the ground at approximately 20-foot
intervals. Flagging and/or streamers shall be placed such that the
flags/streamers move in a light wind.
Vehicular/Pedestrian Traffic - At minimum, one terrain vehicle and/or
one person shall travel throughout the entire disposal area at least
once per hour from dawn to dusk.
rows.normalized: Nest prevention measures must at minimum include flagging/streamers (specs on length, material, stake height/spacing, placement) and vehicular/pedestrian patrol (at least once per hour dawn to dusk); 2 required measures total.

rows.verbatim: Upon the exercise of Option Item "Bird Nesting Prevention Measures", the Contractor shall begin work within 24 hours.
rows.normalized: If Option Item 'Bird Nesting Prevention Measures' is exercised, Contractor must begin work within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: Specific nest prevention measures used during the work shall be monitored for effectiveness and may require adjustment and/or modification.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor nest prevention measures for effectiveness.

rows.verbatim: All equipment/supplies used for nest prevention shall be removed from the work site upon the completion of work and as directed by the Contracting Officer.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove all nest prevention equipment/supplies upon work completion or as directed by CO.

rows.verbatim: If bird nests are discovered at the work site, immediate notification shall be made in accordance with paragraph entitled "Reporting".
rows.normalized: If bird nests are discovered, Contractor must immediately notify per the Reporting paragraph.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall immediately mark the perimeter or boundary of the bird nesting area with flagging on stakes 3-feet above the ground surface and no closer than 3 feet from the nearest nest.

rows.normalized: Contractor must avoid marked area, implement safe work distances, flag exclusion zones, and advise equipment operators of nests/exclusion zones.
